items.title: Fourier multiplier on the Schwartz core
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and n>=1. For a measurable symbol m on R^n define D_m={f in S(R^n): m fhat is locally integrable and its regular distribution is tempered}. For f in D_m put T_m f=F^{-1}(m fhat) in S prime. Frequency products and the inverse are distributional; no Lp boundedness is asserted. D_m is translation stable and T_m commutes with translations tau_a f(x)=f(x-a).
items.strategy: Use the published Schwartz Fourier automorphism and S-prime inverse to define the partial-domain operator. If f is in D_m, multiply m fhat by the smooth bounded exponential exp(-2 pi i a dot xi): it remains a regular tempered distribution. The Schwartz translation identity shows tau_a f is in D_m and F(T_m tau_a f)=exp(-2 pi i a dot xi)m fhat=F(tau_a T_m f). Injectivity gives commutation. The domain qualification prevents an arbitrary measurable symbol from being assumed to act on all Schwartz functions.

items.title: Exact L2 Fourier multiplier norm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. If m is a measurable essentially bounded symbol on R^n, n>=1, then T_m has a unique bounded L2 extension with ||T_m f||_2<=||m||_infinity ||f||_2, and its operator norm equals ess sup |m|. Values on frequency null sets, including {0}, do not affect the operator.
items.strategy: Every Schwartz f is in D_m: m fhat belongs to L2 and the published regular-Lp-to-tempered theorem makes its distribution tempered. Unitary Plancherel conjugates the extension to multiplication M_m on frequency L2, giving the upper bound and uniqueness by Schwartz density. For epsilon>0 below the essential supremum, select a positive finite-measure part E of {|m|>||m||_infinity-epsilon} inside a sufficiently large ball. Its indicator is in L2 and ||m 1_E||_2>(||m||_infinity-epsilon)||1_E||_2. Inverse Plancherel and epsilon to zero give the lower bound. This is an L2 result only.

items.title: Lp Fourier multiplier and its norm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For 1<=p<infinity, a measurable m is an Lp Fourier multiplier if T_m is defined on all Schwartz functions, takes them into Lp(R^n), and ||T_m f||_p<=C||f||_p on that core. Then density gives one unique bounded extension to Lp and ||m||_{M_p}:=||T_m||_{Lp to Lp}. At p=infinity a bounded extension, if chosen, need not be unique from the Schwartz-core action; no intrinsic norm is defined here from that core alone.
items.strategy: C_c-infinity is contained in Schwartz and is dense in complex Lp for finite p under the published density theorem. Thus a core estimate gives a unique bounded extension into complete complex Lp, and the infimum admissible C is its operator norm. For infinity, every Schwartz function vanishes at infinity, so it cannot approximate the constant one in supremum norm; uniqueness of an extension cannot be inferred. The definition makes no Mihlin or endpoint claim.

items.title: Hausdorff–Young for periodic Fourier coefficients
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and normalized Haar measure on T. If 1<=p<=2 and 1/p+1/p_prime=1, every complex f in Lp(T) has Fourier coefficient sequence in ell^{p_prime}(Z) and ||(fhat(k))||_{ell^{p_prime}}<=||f||_{Lp(T)}. At p=1 read ell infinity; at p=2 this is Parseval equality.
items.strategy: On normalized T, |e_k|=1 gives |fhat(k)|<=||f||_1, so the coefficient map is L1 to ell infinity of norm at most one. Published Parseval gives the complex-linear L2 to ell2 isometry, with first-variable-linear coefficient convention. Apply the published sigma-finite finite-simple-core endpoint interpolation corollary to the map on the common core; counting measure on Z and normalized Haar on T are sigma-finite. Countable Choice supplies full-space extension and core density. Check endpoints separately; uniqueness identifies the interpolated map with actual coefficients because each coordinate is an L1-continuous functional on the finite-measure torus.

items.title: Hausdorff–Young for the Euclidean Fourier transform
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Ff(xi)=integral_Rn f(x) exp(-2 pi i x dot xi) dx on L1. For 1<=p<=2, with p_prime conjugate to p, F extends compatibly to a complex-linear bounded map Lp(R^n) to L^{p_prime}(R^n) with ||Ff||_{p_prime}<=||f||_p. At p=1 this is the integral transform, at p=2 the unitary Plancherel transform, and on intersections the interpretations agree.
items.strategy: The published L1 transform estimate is norm at most one to L infinity; published unitary Plancherel is norm one on L2. Their agreement on L1 intersect L2 makes a single complex-linear Schwartz/finite-simple core operator. Apply the endpoint interpolation corollary on sigma-finite Euclidean Lebesgue spaces, obtaining norm <=1 for interior exponents. Extend by complex smooth density and Countable Choice. At endpoints retain the original operators; show compatibility on intersections by simultaneous smooth approximation or the published L1/L2 agreement, and identify the Lp-prime limit independently of approximants.

items.title: Mihlin smoothness convention above half the dimension
items.statement: For n>=1 put q=floor(n/2)+1. A Mihlin symbol here is a measurable m with a C^q representative on R^n minus {0} such that for each multi-index alpha with |alpha|<=q, |partial^alpha m(xi)|<=C_alpha |xi|^{-|alpha|} for xi!=0. The alpha=0 bound includes essential boundedness; m(0) is irrelevant. This is a sufficient symbol condition, with Lp boundedness to be proved on the later singular-integral page for 1<p<infinity.
items.strategy: Define the derivative count and the pointwise punctured-space bounds. Compare Grafakos Theorem 6.2.7: these bounds imply its annular L2 estimates by integrating |xi|^{-2|alpha|} over R<|xi|<2R. Do not invoke that later theorem here or assert endpoint Lp boundedness. W uses the stronger d+2 derivative assumption, so its theorem does not reduce the adopted q.

items.title: Distributional derivatives are polynomial Fourier multipliers
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For u in S prime(R^n) and every multi-index alpha, F(D^alpha u)=(2 pi i xi)^alpha F(u) in S prime. If u and its distribution derivative have L2 representatives, this identity also holds for their Plancherel L2 transforms almost everywhere.
items.strategy: The published tempered Fourier differentiation theorem supplies the distributional identity directly with the exact 2 pi factor and bilinear transposition. For regular L2 u and derivative, invoke published L2-to-S-prime Fourier agreement; equality of regular tempered distributions represented by L2 functions implies equality almost everywhere, using injectivity of the regular-distribution map or Schwartz L2 density. The latter clause needs no as-yet-unpublished PDE W^{k,2} definition.

items.title: Integer-order W^{k,2} and H^k agree with equivalent norms
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For integer k>=0 on R^n, the PDE weak-derivative space W^{k,2} equals the real-order Bessel space H^k as a subset of S prime. The square root of the sum of ||D^alpha u||_2^2 over |alpha|<=k is equivalent to ||<xi>^k uhat||_2; the latter is also equivalent to ||(1+4 pi^2 |xi|^2)^{k/2} uhat||_2, but is generally not identical to either derivative norm.
items.strategy: Using PDE-11’s scaffolded def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm, lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives, lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere, and lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite, identify its weak derivatives with regular L2 distributions. Plancherel and the local polynomial-multiplier lemma turn each derivative norm into ||(2 pi xi)^alpha uhat||_2. For fixed integer k, the finite polynomial P_k(xi)=sum_{|alpha|<=k}(2 pi)^{2|alpha|}|xi^alpha|^2 is bounded above and below by constants times <xi>^{2k}; the lower bound follows from the multinomial expansion of |xi|^{2k} and the alpha=0 term. Compare <xi>^{2k} to (1+4 pi^2|xi|^2)^k by fixed positive constants. Use the batch-12 weighted-distribution theorem for both directions. The four PDE-11 supplier items are declared directly and currently ready at Step 1; Step 3 must independently audit and author them before this consumer is authored.

items.title: Real-order H^s as weighted Fourier distributions
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For every real s and n>=1, PDE-14F H^s(R^n) is canonically exactly {u in S prime: <xi>^s F(u) is a regular L2 distribution}, with norm ||u||_{H^s}=||<xi>^s F(u)||_2. The product on S prime is distributional multiplication by the smooth bracket weight; H^s elements are not initially assumed to be functions.
items.strategy: Invoke batch-12 weighted-distribution characterization with its canonical embedding E_s and its unique L2 class g. Its two directions identify every completion class and every qualifying tempered distribution, and its isometry gives the exact defining norm. Retain the batch-12 distributional multiplication convention; neither replace the bracket by the 2 pi Laplacian weight nor infer pointwise Fourier values before obtaining g.

items.title: Japanese-bracket and Laplacian Bessel-potential operators
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On S prime define <D>^t u=F^{-1}(<xi>^t F(u)) for real t, where <xi>=(1+|xi|^2)^{1/2}. Separately define (I-Delta)^{t/2}u by the symbol (1+4 pi^2|xi|^2)^{t/2}. Both are continuous, invertible Fourier multipliers on S prime. Their symbols differ for t!=0 under the negative-sign 2 pi transform.
items.strategy: The batch-12 bracket lemma proves smooth polynomially bounded derivatives for <xi>^{plus/minus t} and their inverse actions on S prime. The same chain-rule calculation with 4 pi^2|xi|^2 gives the corresponding bounds for the Laplacian symbol and its reciprocal; the published smooth multiplier lemma supplies continuous transposed actions. Published Fourier differentiation gives F(I-Delta)u=(1+4 pi^2|xi|^2)F(u) for integer powers, fixing the functional-calculus notation. Inverse Fourier exists on S prime; compare the two weights at any nonzero frequency to distinguish them.

items.title: Bessel potentials shift Sobolev order
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For every real s,t, <D>^t:H^s(R^n) to H^{s-t}(R^n) is a surjective linear isometry with inverse <D>^{-t}. The operator (I-Delta)^{t/2} is a bounded isomorphism between the same spaces with equivalent norms; under the fixed H^s bracket norm it is not generally an isometry when t!=0. Moreover H^s embeds contractively in H^r whenever s>=r, and each distributional partial_j maps H^{s+1} boundedly into H^s with operator norm at most 2 pi.
items.strategy: For u in H^s, multiply its Fourier distribution by <xi>^t; the target weighted L2 representative is <xi>^{s-t}<xi>^t F(u)=<xi>^s F(u), proving exact norm equality and membership. Reciprocal multiplier <xi>^{-t} gives surjectivity. For the Laplacian operator, the ratio r_t(xi)=((1+4 pi^2|xi|^2)/(1+|xi|^2))^{t/2} has positive finite lower and upper bounds; hence the target norm is equivalent. At xi=0 the ratio is 1 and its high-frequency limit is (2 pi)^t, so for t!=0 a frequency-localized L2 test disproves a universal isometry. For s>=r the pointwise weight ratio <xi>^{r-s}<=1 gives the contractive inclusion. The derivative multiplier has |2 pi xi_j|<=2 pi<xi>, giving ||partial_j u||_{H^s}<=2 pi||u||_{H^{s+1}}; use the local tempered derivative identity to identify the target distribution.

items.title: Conjugate duality of H^s and H^{-s}
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and use the first-variable-linear complex L2 inner product. Let the conjugate dual of H^s mean bounded conjugate-linear functionals on H^s. For v in H^{-s} define A_v(u)=integral_Rn overline(F(u)(xi)) F(v)(xi) dxi, interpreted as the L2 pairing of <xi>^s F(u) with <xi>^{-s}F(v). Then v to A_v is a complex-linear isometric bijection H^{-s} onto that conjugate dual. The ordinary linear dual is obtained by conjugating this pairing and is conjugate-linear in v.
items.strategy: Write g=J_su and h=J_{-s}v in complex L2. Since the Fourier weights cancel, A_v(u)=integral overline(g)h, an absolutely convergent sesquilinear pairing. Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||A_v||<=||h||_2. For h!=0, surjectivity of J_s allows g=h/||h||_2, giving the reverse bound. For any bounded conjugate-linear A on H^s, B(u)=overline(A(u)) is a bounded linear functional; the published first-variable-linear Hilbert Riesz theorem gives a representing vector w in H^s. Transport its weighted Fourier representative through J_s, conjugate as needed, and use surjectivity of J_{-s} to obtain a unique v with A=A_v. The zero case is direct. This pairing extends the L2 conjugate pairing on Schwartz tests, not a bilinear distribution action on arbitrary H^s pairs.

title: Fourier Multipliers and Sobolev Characterisations — Examples

items.title: Heat and Poisson semigroups as Fourier multipliers
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For t>=0 define the heat operator H_t on L2(R^n) by the Fourier symbol exp(-4 pi^2 t|xi|^2), and the Poisson operator P_t by exp(-2 pi t|xi|). These Fourier-defined operators, customarily denoted e^{t Delta} and e^{-t sqrt{-Delta}}, are L2 contractions, equal identity at t=0, and obey T_tT_r=T_{t+r} in each family; for t>0 their solutions satisfy the heat and upper-half-space Laplace equations respectively.
items.strategy: Use F(Delta f)=-4 pi^2|xi|^2 Ff from the published derivative identity. For the heat equation, the scalar frequency ODE gives e^{-4 pi^2 t|xi|^2}; for U_tt+Delta_x U=0 choose the decaying frequency branch e^{-2 pi t|xi|}. At t>0 frequency differentiation is justified in L2 by boundedness of |xi|^j times the decaying exponent for the required orders. Multiplication of symbols proves composition, their absolute values are <=1, and dominated convergence plus Plancherel gives strong L2 continuity at zero. Avoid claiming the nonsmooth Poisson symbol preserves Schwartz at xi=0.

items.title: Translation and differentiation symbols
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For tau_a f(x)=f(x-a) on Schwartz space, its multiplier symbol is exp(-2 pi i a dot xi) and tau_a is an L2 isometry. The distributional derivative partial_j has symbol 2 pi i xi_j; for n>=1 this unbounded symbol gives no bounded L2 extension of partial_j from Schwartz space.
items.strategy: Substitute y=x-a in the Schwartz Fourier integral to obtain F(tau_a f)=e^{-2 pi i a dot xi}Ff. Its modulus is one, so the exact L2 multiplier bound makes tau_a an isometry. The published distribution derivative identity gives F(partial_j f)=2 pi i xi_j Ff. For each N choose a nonzero smooth compactly supported frequency bump in {|xi_j|>N}; inverse Schwartz Fourier transforms it to f_N. Plancherel yields ||partial_j f_N||_2>=2 pi N||f_N||_2, disproving a bounded L2 extension. No Mihlin conclusion is invoked.

items.title: Fefferman ball multiplier obstruction
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the library Fourier and Lp conventions. Recorded boundary result (not proved here): for n>=2, the characteristic function of a Euclidean ball is an Lp(R^n) Fourier multiplier only at p=2 in the usual 1<=p<infinity range. This deep theorem is a bibliographic leaf and does not supply any proof on this page.
items.strategy: Fefferman Theorem 1 on printed p. 330 states that the ball multiplier is bounded only on L2 when n>1. The local L2 case follows from the exact multiplier lemma; the p!=2 obstruction needs Fefferman Kakeya geometry and is recorded, not used as a dependency or claimed proved here. The source PDF is a scanned eight-page article; its statement page was inspected visually.

items.title: Jump multipliers may lie outside the Mihlin criterion
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the library Fourier and Lp conventions. Recorded orientation result (not proved here): in one dimension the shifted signum symbol m(xi)=sgn(xi-1) has a jump at the nonzero frequency 1, so it fails the punctured-domain Mihlin condition, yet it is bounded on Lp(R) for 1<p<infinity as a modulation conjugate of the Hilbert-transform multiplier. In contrast, unshifted sgn(xi) satisfies the stated one-dimensional Mihlin condition because its only jump is at the excluded origin. The Lp bound is proved later in FR-8, not used here.
items.strategy: On R minus {0}, unshifted signum is locally constant and has zero derivatives, so it meets q=1 Mihlin bounds. The translated symbol sgn(xi-1) is discontinuous at xi=1 and therefore fails C^1 away from zero. Frequency translation of a multiplier corresponds to conjugating its operator by physical modulation, preserving Lp norm; combine this elementary identity with the later Hilbert-transform Lp theorem to establish the recorded positive boundedness claim. Neither later theorem is a proof supplier for this page. This corrects the design’s false assertion about unshifted signum while retaining its intended outside-Mihlin example.

items.title: A Dirac mass has precisely sufficiently negative Sobolev order
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. In R^n, n>=1, the Dirac mass delta_0 belongs to H^s if and only if s<-n/2. The endpoint s=-n/2 fails by logarithmic divergence.
items.strategy: The published tempered Fourier calculation gives F(delta_0)=1. The batch-12 weighted criterion reduces membership to integral_Rn(1+|xi|^2)^s dxi<infinity. Near zero the integrand is bounded above and below, so only infinity matters. The published polar-coordinate integration formula gives convergence exactly when integral_1^infinity r^{n-1+2s}dr converges, i.e. 2s+n<0. At equality it is the harmonic integral of dr/r and diverges logarithmically. No pointwise-function assumption on delta_0 is made.
